thread:
maria: Heads up — after pushing nvidia-driver 536.12 to the us-west GPU pool we started seeing ~10% of nodes fail to boot (hang in dracut) with DKMS rebuild errors. Anyone else seeing this? :rotating_light:

sam: Yep seeing the same in eu-central but smaller. Logs show 'Required signature not found' and 'modpost: ERROR: could not find module.signing_key' — smells like Secure Boot + unsigned modules.

leo: Confirmed on two hosts: Secure Boot enforced, DKMS attempted to rebuild but couldn't sign modules. Excerpt from kernel log:

```
[    4.123456] modpost: ERROR: could not find module.signing_key
[    4.123457] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[    4.125000] systemd[1]: dracut-initqueue timeout - kicking other processes
```

olivia: We saw regressions with 525 previously but were able to rollback quickly. This one is weird because the 536 package should ship signed modules. Which kernel ABI are affected?

ppatel: Most failures are on nodes running kernels between 6.1.0-9 and 6.2.x (mixed across cloud images and a couple on our on-prem hosts). Full dkms build log snippet:

```
DKMS: build started for nvidia-536.12
make[1]: Entering directory '/usr/src/nvidia-536.12/kernel'
make: *** No rule to make target 'modules_install'. Stop.
ERROR: Cannot create compiled module for kernel 6.2.8
modpost: ERROR: could not find module.signing_key
```

engops-bot: deploybot: Rollout event: 2026-02-12T15:02:00Z - nvidia-driver: 536.12 pushed to 120 nodes (us-west), 30 nodes (eu-central). Status: partially successful -> rolling paused.

maria: Action plan (short):
1) Pause the rest of the rollout — done.
2) Cordon/drain affected nodes and move workloads to fallback pool.
3) Roll back the us-west GPU pool to the 535.101 image.
4) Produce prebuilt, signed kernel modules for 536 and add them to the image build pipeline.

sam: We can't toggle Secure Boot via cloud provider for some instance types; on-prem we can. For detection we can run 'mokutil --sb-state' and check for 'SecureBoot enabled'.

```
# quick check
ssh node-123
sudo mokutil --sb-state || true
```

leo: Short-term workaround: taint/cordon affected nodes so scheduler avoids them, spin up new node pool with the older driver AMI (535.101). Example commands we used earlier:

```
kubectl cordon node-123
kubectl drain node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# create new node pool with image: redwood-gpu-ami-535-2026-01
```

olivia: I've opened a support case with NVIDIA for module signing and possible kernel ABI changes in 536. Also preparing a DKMS patch to include a fallback to pre-signed modules when secureboot is enabled. Will test on staging eu-central pool.

ppatel: Operational impact estimate: ~120 nodes affected in us-west, rollout paused. Remediation (rollback + node recycle) ~6-12 hours. Emergency cost for extra fallback nodes ~ $1.5k/day if we keep them up. Adding as cost note for infra ops.

sam: Postmortem action items: add kernel-driver compatibility check to release checklist, gate driver rollouts with Secure Boot test image, publish prebuilt signed artifacts for major driver releases, and add automated detection for unsigned modules during AMI bake. :thumbsup:

maria: If anyone spots an uncordoned failing node, drop the node name here. I'll start the rollback and coordinate with SRE on autoscaler policies. Thanks all.
